title: kith-tslocal: decode Peer nodes from LocalAPI /status
description:
The Tailscale /status response contains a Peer map keyed by node key, but kith-tslocal currently only decodes the local node's tailnet IPs. Add decoding of peer nodes so the discovery task can enumerate all tailnet peers.

What: Extend StatusResponse to decode the Peer map.

Algorithm:
1. Add a new struct PeerNode:
   - user_id: String  (from UserID field, use deserialize_as_string like SelfPeer)
   - login_name: String  (from UserProfile.LoginName or Peer.DNSName, see note)
   - display_name: Option<String>  (from UserProfile.DisplayName)
   - dns_name: String  (from DNSName, e.g. 'alice-laptop.tail-xxxxx.ts.net.')
   - tailscale_ips: Vec<String>  (from TailscaleIPs)

   Note: Tailscale /status Peer entries have: UserID (integer), DNSName (MagicDNS with trailing dot), TailscaleIPs, Hostinfo.OS, etc. LoginName is on the top-level User map keyed by UserID. For simplicity: use DNSName as the display login fallback; the discovery task will get login from the probed kithd session anyway.

2. Add peers: HashMap<String, PeerNode> to StatusResponse (key = node key, value = PeerNode).
   Use #[serde(rename = 'Peer', default)] to ignore missing field if no peers.

3. Add a helper method status_peers(&self) -> Vec<&PeerNode> that deduplicates by user_id and skips the local node (compare user_id to self_node.user_id).

4. Add unit tests with hardcoded JSON (not from live Tailscale):
   - Test 1: status with two peers; assert peers map has 2 entries with correct user_ids
   - Test 2: status with no peers (empty map); assert peers returns empty Vec
   - Test 3: status_peers deduplicates same user_id across multiple nodes

Defensive programming rules:
- Default all new fields (missing fields should not fail deserialization)
- Strip trailing dot from dns_name on deserialization (Tailscale appends '.')
- PeerNode user_id uses same deserialize_as_string as SelfPeer (handles numeric IDs)
- No logging of user IDs
